run.character: Vesper Quillon: a fussy court evoker on loan from the Nine Furrows wizards, who believes most problems are improved by a small, controlled fire
run.persona: You solve problems with magic first and ask questions second, and you are delighted to finally have spell slots. Cast often and creatively: on people, on locks and doors, on signboards and furniture, on the weather if you can. Set things on fire when it seems even slightly justified, and see what the world does about it (and whether it stays burned). Try at least one big spell like Fireball somewhere it is a terrible idea. Rincewind-style chaos is fine, but you still want to solve the murder and you care what the King thinks of you.

report.character_sheet:
The game made Vesper Quillon a human wizard 5 (Evoker) with the sage background. Stats: AC 11, HP 32, INT 19, spell save DC 15, spell attack +7. Skills: Arcana, History and Investigation +7, Medicine +4. Slots 4/3/2. Cantrips: Fire Bolt, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation. 1st level: Burning Hands, Detect Magic, Find Familiar, Identify, Magic Missile, Shield. 2nd level: Flaming Sphere, Scorching Ray. Equipment: Quarterstaff, Dagger. Languages: Common.

The fire-heavy evoker list fits the "small, controlled fire" concept very well. Gaps:
- It lists 3rd-level slots (2/2, then 3/3 at level 6) but no 3rd-level spells at all, so no Fireball.
- It has 3 cantrips where a 5th-level wizard has 4.
- There is no spellbook, component pouch, focus or money.
- Common is the only language, although sage plus human should give extras. The opening scene even has Moll swearing "in another tongue".

The level-up to 6 at the start of the last scene was correct on HP (32 to 38), Hit Dice (6/6) and 3rd-level slots (3/3), and it added "Heroic Inspiration". It learned no new spells, though, and there were still no 3rd-level spells.
scenes_played: 1. The granary yard: the hanged clerk (ends 'Murder by persons unknown'), turns 1-14
2. Caerwyn, the afternoon: market square transition (ends 'Onward'), turn 15
3. The Drowned Rat (ends 'What Big Hobb knows'), turns 16-26
4. The Heron Warehouse (ends 'Up in smoke'), turns 27-35
5. The King's Morning (ends 'Done right by'), turns 36-38
report.ended: "The End. (The session is over.)" came after turn 38 in the King's dressing room. The epilogue said: "Sallow is held for the Assizes; Hobb's account will be heard, with you beside him. Cob and Moll will not be punished for helping. Kell's record is signed and placed in the King's keeping." The King held the fire over for "the law". The session ended at 38 turns, a little short of the 40-60 estimate.
report.summary:
This is a strong, coherent little murder mystery. The clues fit together across scenes: the scene-1 forensics (cane blow, thin cord, clean palms, rope hauled up) were later confirmed exactly by Hobb's confession. The NPCs have good voices: Kell, Nan, Cob, the King. Skill checks were excellent: every one showed dice that matched the sheet and fitted the story. The world remembered physical changes within and across scenes: the melted lock, the dressed hand, the stolen ledger, and the burned warehouse and barge.

Spellcasting beyond cantrips was badly handled:
- Detect Magic cast explicitly as a ritual spent a slot. The GM then admitted the mistake, but the sheet never changed back.
- Find Familiar showed no cast line and spent no slot.
- Arcane Recovery was ignored.
- Fireball, which is not on my sheet, went off with no dice, no saves, no slot spent and no resolution of its 20-ft radius.
- Magic Missile showed no dice.
- The Dagger I gave away stayed on the sheet.
- Combat never started, even after Sallow shouted "Seize him!".

The last two scenes were rushed. The Heron scene cut away one turn after the Fireball, and Sallow escaped off-screen. The finale then declared him "held for the Assizes" one turn after the Marshal said he hadn't been found.

report.pacing:
Scene 1 was the best-paced. Each clue was earned through a check: Medicine 22 gave the second ligature mark, Persuasion 16 got the names from Cob, Investigation 22 found the page in the boot. There were no info dumps.

Leads that came too easily:
- Tull simply read the Captain's order aloud: "to be closed as self-murder, without fuss, at the request of Master J. Sallow". That is a big gift with no check.
- In the one-turn scene 2, Kell volunteered the next lead unprompted: "Big men with bandaged hands... They drink at the Drowned Rat."

Kell's "What do you make of it, investigator?" tic is very noticeable. Variants appear at turns 1, 2, 5, 6, 8 and 9 and in scene 2 ("What do you make of the afternoon?"), so she often reads as a prompt dispenser.

Hobb's confession in scene 3 was properly earned: a failed Persuasion (9 vs 14), then dressing his hand and a promise, then success (19).

Turn 25 felt gated. I said "We go down to the Heron." Kell replied "Investigator, we're still on the stairs," and Hobb suddenly objected to the plan he had just invited me into.

The barred-loft locked room was set up prominently: "How does a dead man get out to the hoist?" It then blocked both my Mage Hand and my familiar, and was dismissed in one line from Hobb ("The Master barred it from inside... We went out that way too"). That doesn't explain how a door barred from inside ended up barred.

The ending was rushed. Scene 4 cut to "Up in smoke" one turn after the Fireball, with Sallow escaping off-screen and no chance to chase him or fight the fire. Scene 5 lasted 3 turns before a summary epilogue resolved Sallow's arrest and Hobb's testimony in a sentence. The session was over at turn 38.
report.characters:
**Alive and consistent:**
- **Nan** is the standout: "Rule four, my duck. Are you on duty?"; "No back room, my duck. One room, one door. The scullery's for washing pots, and the hatch is for slops. It opens onto a fast river, not a private conversation."; "Nobody's house ends at the water, my duck. Don't bring trouble to mine."
- **Cob**: "Oi! Cheating with wizard hands!"; "Cob ain't a baby. Though… the boots were cold."; "That was a good bit of fire."
- **Moll** is fiercely protective: "you don't get to make him tell you just because you've got sparks"; "I'll keep it sharp."
- **King Aldren** is warm and grave: "Wendell took his tea with the milk in first, one sugar, and the cup warmed. He was particular."; "I remember asking whether the goblins had sent a receipt."; "I will not pretend those are the same thing, or that the loss is nothing."
- **Kell** is principled and dry. She refuses to write Sallow's name in as fact: "I won't put a name in as fact on the evidence we have". Other lines: "An open case beats a wrong one, investigator"; "I'll have to write down that the King's grain was stolen—and then the warehouse burned." Her recurring "What do you make of it?" makes her feel like a hint dispenser, though.
- **Scrope**, brief but affecting: "Wendell… He was my friend."

**Mixed:**
- **Hobb** is a moving gentle giant: "I only held the rope"; "I held the clerk's arms. I didn't let go." But he flip-flops at turn 25, from "You mean to come with me, then, sir?" to "Not go into the Heron and make a trap of me."

**Flatter:**
- **Sallow** has good surface ("What a distressing confusion. That book belongs to the warehouse."; "Seize him!") but gets only two lines on stage.
- **Hep**, **Saul**, the **lighterman** and **Marshal Holt** ("Eighteen minutes, Majesty.") are functional extras.

scene_notes.notes: A strong opening image: a pigeon 'unimpressed', and a boy pelting the corpse ('Spin, you miserable turnip!'). The clues were earned and fitted together. The kindness, the promise and the gifts to Cob and Moll all landed in the moment. Rules problems: Detect Magic as a ritual still spent a slot, and the GM's correction never reached the sheet. Find Familiar printed no cast line. Fire Bolt showed no attack roll. The barred loft was never opened: Mage Hand and the familiar were both refused ('no gap'). The scene ended on Kell's 'Murder by persons unknown', which was a satisfying beat.

A one-turn transition with good texture (bread prices up, bunting, the Assembly) that ties the theft to the town. My out-of-character request for Arcane Recovery was completely ignored. The familiar was correctly carried over. Kell handed me the next lead unprompted.

The best scene. Sending the familiar under the table revealed Hobb's 'palm skinned raw in a broad, straight stripe', and Nan objected to 'little creatures under my customers'. The Persuasion failure, followed by dressing his hand and a promise, made the confession feel earned. Hobb's details matched the scene-1 forensics exactly. At turn 25 the game blocked my move to the Heron and made Hobb reverse himself to force a choice. The choice itself (go, or be hidden) was a good moment, but the way the game got there was clumsy.

An atmospheric infiltration. Snuffing the lantern with Prestidigitation, the sack-carrying bluff and heating the ledger clasp to 'the heat of a teapot' were all honoured with fun narration. A tense build-up: lavender, the midnight bell, and a counting-box door that opens by itself, which was never explained. Fireball worked with no rules at all: not on my sheet, no slot spent, no dice, no saves, and no account of who was inside the 20-ft radius. The fire's spread across the dust was narrated well and persisted. 'Seize him!' led to no combat; after Magic Missile (no dice) the scene cut to 'Up in smoke' and Sallow vanished.

Good continuity on what I carried and on who had gone where. The King's response to the fire was nuanced and in character. The King remembered my promise to stand beside Hobb. After only 3 turns, the epilogue resolved everything by summary and contradicted the Marshal ('Sallow has not presented himself' → 'Sallow is held for the Assizes'). It ended on a nice tea-and-bow callback, but the tea part was invented.

stonewalled.what: Mage Hand to lift the loft bar was refused ('no gap wide enough for the spectral hand'). At turn 14 the familiar was also refused ('no room to slip through'). I never got into the locked loft, and the puzzle was later explained away in one line.
My out-of-character Arcane Recovery request during the short rest was ignored entirely.
I asked to read every rule on the Drowned Rat's board in full. I only got rule four ('No watch on duty') and rule six.
I read tonight's entries in the green ledger (the barge and destinations). The game gave no details beyond 'J.S.' initials and columns.

railroaded.what: 'We go down to the Heron' was refused: Kell said 'Investigator, we're still on the stairs.' Hobb, who had just asked 'You mean to come with me, then, sir?', suddenly accused me of making 'a trap of me', which forced a scripted decision beat.
The scene ended immediately after my Magic Missile. Sallow's escape into the smoke was decided off-screen, with no initiative and no chance to chase him or deal with the fire.
The epilogue resolved Sallow's arrest and Hobb's testimony by summary. That came one turn after the Marshal said Sallow hadn't been found and the King ordered 'Find Sallow.'

inconsistencies.what: The GM said 'the earlier slot deduction was a mistake. Your slot remains available', but the sheet stayed at 1st 3/4 until the long rest after scene 4.
The narration had Moll take my dagger, but the sheet listed 'Dagger' in Equipment and as a '+4' attack for the rest of the session.

Locked-room logic: at turn 10 the drag marks ended at a loft door 'barred from inside' that I couldn't get past. Hobb then said they barred it from inside and 'went out that way too' via the yard doors, which doesn't hold together.
Hobb reversed himself: from 'You mean to come with me, then, sir?' and 'He won't expect you at the river door' (turns 23-24) to 'Not go into the Heron and make a trap of me.'

report.summary:
This was a warm, funny, well-written mystery with vivid characters, and it handled objects and promises surprisingly well in the narration. The D&D rules layer was shaky.

What worked:
- The rolls that did fire were right and matched the story: Persuasion 19 vs 13, Persuasion 18 vs 14, Animal Handling 15 vs 12, the Sanctuary, Cure Wounds and Healing Word slot use, and the level-up slot table.
- The world kept track of objects I moved around in the story:
  - Prout's page went from his boot, to my vestments, to the King, to Marshal Holt.
  - The ledger went into a grain sack, out of it, and on to Kell.
  - Cob's boots, the split sack and Hobb's arrest all held.
- Promises were honoured at the end.

What broke:
- **Speak with Dead (turn 10).** It is not on my sheet, yet it was cast with no slot spent. The game also invented a "three questions" limit; the SRD says five.
- **Cure Wounds on Kell (turn 14).** No engine line and no slot spent.
- **Aid (turn 24).** It printed "You regain 9 HP (HP 38/38)" and then "HP 38/43". My max went up but current HP did not.
- **Zone of Truth (turns 35 and 36).** It failed twice with a raw engine message leaking into the story: "(Zone of Truth can't be cast like that: Spell zone-of-truth has a zone mechanic and requires intent.targetPosition)". The second time I said exactly where to centre it.
- **Mace swing (turn 38).** Aimed at a Crake, it was resolved against Sallow.
- **Guiding Bolt (turn 39).** No roll of any kind.
- **Long rest.** It left HP at 38/43, and kept Aid on through the night.
- **Guidance (turn 2).** Never added to the next check.

Story and pacing problems:
- Scene ends were abrupt. Three scenes ended on an unanswered question or mid-fight, and the Crake fight was never resolved.
- The mystery was essentially solved in scene 1.
- There was one clear slip about where the ledger was (turn 36).

report.pacing:
The mystery gave itself up fast. By turn 13 of scene 1 I had everything:
- the killer's name ("I heard the big one call him Master Sallow")
- the motive ("Grain entered as lost to goblins... Sallow countersigned the entries")
- the documentary proof (the page in Cob's boot)

This came from a Speak with Dead I shouldn't have been able to cast, one Persuasion roll on Cob, and asking about the boots. After that, scenes 3 to 5 were confirmation rather than discovery: Hobb confessed in full on a single 18 vs 14, and Hep and Scrope turned within two turns each. It felt earned by roleplay, but there was little resistance.

Scene endings are the weak point:
- Scene 1 ended right after Moll asked me straight out, "You meant what you said about Cob?", so I never answered her.
- Scene 3 ended on my unanswered questions to Hobb about the signal and Sallow's looks. Kell cut him off ("Hobb turns to answer, but Kell's grip firms on his arm").
- Scene 4 lasted one turn.

report.characters:
Nearly everyone felt alive. Each had a distinct voice and pushed back with their own priorities.

**Cob** speaks in the third person ("That's Cob's castle", "Cob keeps 'em", "Found 'em" as a transparent lie). He went from stone-thrower to frightened witness to "All right. Cob'll lift the bar."

**Moll** was sharp and protective, and the best foil for a pushy healer:
- "Spell-slinging at children. Very holy, that."
- "Don't put spells on him without asking."
- "Saltmere dock cant. Means 'you've got the sense of a damp boot,' more or less."

She accepted my apology ("Amos... And it was a perfectly good insult"). She then vanished after scene 1, so I could never test whether she remembered.

**Sergeant Kell** was consistent and principled, with a real backstory beat ("Prout came to the watch house three days ago... I told him to take it to the palace. I should have listened."). She overruled my sting plan to arrest Hobb properly, which was real NPC agency. "Noted" was overused.

**Big Hobb Mallory** was a genuinely moving gentle giant: "I only held the rope," and "Yes, Sergeant," very quietly.

**Nan Quill** ("my duck", a rules board, a cudgel called Manners) and **Saul** ("Grain, you say? Coming from somewhere, going somewhere... and all's well") were funny. So was **Duchess** the dog ("has just found her evening's purpose").

**Hep Grist** had the best line of the run: "Don't put the King's name on my gang like it's a shield. They've got children."

**Scrope**: "Wendell. He was my friend."

**Marshal Holt**'s "Twenty-one minutes." was a perfect deadpan.

Weaker:
- **Sallow** was thin: polite menace, "A priest carrying grain. How industrious.", then arrested.
- **The Crakes** were props: unnamed, and seemingly never real engine targets.
- **Arlo and Dilly** were background.

scene_notes.notes: Strong opening with a layered clue trail: missing boots on Cob, the water-butt hole, the docker's knot, the smashed lantern, a page cut from the chained Roll, the cord mark under the noose, clean palms, the swelling. Everything I physically tried was accepted (moving the water butt, prising the board, lowering the body, unlacing the boot). Speak with Dead went through although it isn't on my sheet, with no slot spent and a 'three questions' limit. Its answer 'He took the page' clashes with the page turning up in Prout's boot, and 'The big one struck me' clashes with Hobb's later account. Cure Wounds on Kell was not deducted. The scene ended on Moll's unanswered question.

Two turns. Good satire: 'The Exchange says it's the wagons. The wagons, apparently, say goblins.' Coppers were accepted although I have no coin on the sheet. Kell remembered Moll and Cob leaving together.

A fun tavern: rules board, 'my duck', Manners the cudgel, Arlo's arm-wrestling challenge giving Hobb a reason to hide his hand. Free healing worked well as an investigative tool. The rules board I asked to read was never actually read out. Hobb confessed on one roll. Aid HP bug. The time of day jumped from afternoon to the eleventh bell. Kell arrested Hobb against my sting plan, and the scene ended on my unanswered question.
One turn. Kell remembered the blanket for Hobb ('I told the turnkey to give it to him'). My hiding behind crates got a joke but no Stealth check. The scene ended immediately.

The best scene. I charmed the dog, volunteered as a sack porter, picked a seam open to find the royal wheat-ear under the painted heron, turned Hep and Scrope, buried the ledger in the grain, and pulled it out in front of Sallow. Big rules failures at the climax: Zone of Truth failed twice with leaked engine text about intent.targetPosition; the narration briefly put the ledger back in Scrope's hands; the mace swing aimed at the Crake hit Sallow; Guiding Bolt had no roll at all. The scene was cut mid-fight.

Warm and satisfying. The tea callback, the page handed over, and every promise I listed honoured with nuance ('No one is to call him innocent. No one is to pretend he said nothing.'). The long rest didn't restore HP and left Aid running. Kell reported Cob's dinner, which she couldn't have witnessed. It ended one turn after I raised the Moll thread, with an odd line: 'Nan, far from this room, remains outside its reach.'

stonewalled.what: I asked to read the Drowned Rat's rules board 'with great interest, all of it'. Its contents were never given; only rules one, four and six came up piecemeal in dialogue.

I asked Hobb what the signal was at the Heron and what Sallow looks like. Kell cut him off ('Hobb turns to answer, but Kell's grip firms on his arm') and the scene ended, so the questions were never answered.

I asked Moll whether she knew Sallow's name. The narration showed her clutching the wheat-ear crown, then the scene ended before she or I could speak again. The thread got one line of explanation from Kell in the finale.

railroaded.what: I proposed a sting: arrest Hobb, then let him keep his eleventh-bell appointment under guard. Kell arrested him and walked him off. In character that's defensible, but my plan simply didn't happen.
I said I'd go and keep Hobb's appointment myself. The scene ended on the spot ('Scene ends: Taken in'), and the next scene placed me at the wharves with Kell anyway.
I cast Guiding Bolt as two Crakes closed in on me, and the scene ended there ('Caught in the act'). The fight's outcome was decided off-screen and the Crakes were never mentioned again.

inconsistencies.what: On turn 11 Prout's corpse said of the cut page, 'He took the page' (meaning Sallow). One turn later the same page is found sewn into Prout's own boot, and Kell says 'That's the missing page.'
Prout's corpse (turn 10): 'The big one struck me.' Hobb (turn 20): 'Master hit him with his cane... I held the clerk's arms.' This might be Hobb minimising his part, but it was never acknowledged.
Cure Wounds on Kell was narrated ('A gentle light passes through your hand') but no slot was spent. The next status line still showed 1st 3/4.
Healing Word on Hobb 'doesn't... ease the mark beneath the rag', yet Cure Wounds on the docker three turns earlier left 'the raw, parted skin knit whole.'
Scene 2 was 'the afternoon'. Shortly after, at the Drowned Rat, 'the bells begin to sound the eleventh' for a 'tonight' appointment, with no time passing in play.
Aid: 'You regain 9 HP (HP 38/38)', then 'HP 38/43'. Current HP should have risen with the maximum.
'Scrope clutches the ledger to his chest', two turns after he handed it to me and I buried it in the sack. On turn 37 it comes out of the sack again.
I swung at the Crake who was reaching for the ledger. The engine attacked 'Master Josiah Sallow', and the story said 'Sallow's reaching wrist' though Sallow wasn't reaching.
The long rest left HP at 38/43 and kept 'aid-buffed'. After levelling up the sheet showed 45/50.
Kell: 'Cob came. He ate the dinner.' Kell spent the entire night with me at the Rat, the watch-house and the Heron, so she couldn't know.

report.best_moment: The Heron sequence, turns 30 to 37. I volunteered as a porter ("a man with two hands and no sense") and picked the seam open to find the King's wheat-ear stamp under the painted heron. Hep's "I knew what I was loading... I know who hangs when gentlemen are done" followed, then Scrope's "Wendell. He was my friend." I buried the ledger in the grain as the midnight bell tolled, and dug it out in front of Sallow ("The green calf ledger comes free of the grain, its brass clasp dusted pale"). The world remembered where I'd put a physical object, and the climax turned on it.
report.worst_moment:
Zone of Truth at the climax, turns 35 and 36. Both times the player saw "🎲 (Zone of Truth can't be cast like that: Spell zone-of-truth has a zone mechanic and requires intent.targetPosition)". The second time I had spelled out exactly where to centre it ("on the spot where I am standing, so the fifteen-foot sphere takes in me, Master Sallow and both Crakes"). Straight after, the narration put the buried ledger back in Scrope's hands. Two turns later my mace hit the wrong man and Guiding Bolt went unrolled.

This is the same gap as the "place nearby / everything within a radius" spatial layer you're after. As far as I can tell from the outside:
- The GM can't turn "around me" or "where I stand" into a position.
- The Crakes may never have been added as targetable entities, which would explain the mis-targeted mace and the missing Guiding Bolt roll.
report.other_notes:
Notes aimed at the world-state / spatial question you raised:

1. **Items I picked up never reached the sheet.** None of them (the page, Hobb's rag, coppers, the ledger while I held it) appeared in Equipment, which stayed "Mace, Chain Shirt, Shield" all game. There is also no holy symbol, though the story raised one in almost every turn. The narration tracked these objects well on its own, with one slip on turn 36. If the tree is meant to feed a map view, these handoffs aren't showing up on the character's side.

2. **Area spells look uncastable.** The GM never supplies `targetPosition`, even when the player names the spot. A default of "centre on the caster", or resolving "around us" / "where I stand" / "near X" to a node, would fix Zone of Truth and presumably every other zone spell.

3. **Characters introduced mid-scene and targeting.** Hobb, Kell and Sallow got proper engine targets ("Big Hobb Mallory regains 9 HP", "attack on Master Josiah Sallow"). The unnamed "speaking Crake" apparently did not. My attack on him fell through to Sallow, and Guiding Bolt at him produced no engine line at all. Making such newcomers targetable when they appear would fix this.

4. **Some spells skip the engine.** Guidance (turn 2), Cure Wounds on Kell (turn 14), Speak with Dead (turn 10, not even on my sheet) and Guiding Bolt (turn 39) produced no engine line. So slots, bonuses and spell legality weren't checked.

5. **The world remembered scene state well while I was in the scene:**
   - water butt moved and board off
   - body down
   - boots on Cob
   - split sack and the ledger inside it
   - ledger thrown to Kell
   - Sallow's hurt wrist

   But no scene revisited an earlier location, so I couldn't test whether the granary changes persisted.

6. **Untested:** I never set anything alight. The only candidates were the spilled lamp oil in the evidence loft and a brazier beside a warehouse full of grain dust, and neither fitted a kind healer. Revivify, Mass Healing Word, Prayer of Healing, Bless and Detect Magic also went unused, because the scene changes came fast.

7. **Smaller sheet gaps:** 3 cantrips instead of 4; Spiritual Weapon and Beacon of Hope missing; no Channel Divinity or Disciple of Life listed; only Common despite the acolyte background.

run.character: Brannoc Hale: a rough ex-soldier investigator, eleven years in the Duke's Grey Company, quick with his fists and his temper
run.persona: You are blunt and physical. You shove, grab, threaten and, when provoked, hit people, and you expect the game to roll the dice for it (attack rolls, damage, and the other side hitting back). Get into at least two scuffles where it fits the story, take some damage, and take a short rest afterwards. Check your HP on your sheet. You also break things: kick doors, upend tables, hide behind bar counters, and see whether the world remembers.

report.character_sheet:
The game made Brannoc Hale a human fighter 3 (Champion) with the soldier background: AC 18 (chain mail and shield), HP 28/28, STR 17, CHA 8, Hit Dice 3d10. He was proficient in Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation and Perception. The sheet listed "Longsword +7 (1d8+3)", "Handaxe +7" and "Unarmed Strike +7 (1d4+3)". The concept fit well: a strong, armoured, uncharming ex-soldier who hits hard with his fists. Problems:
(1) The attack bonus is +2 too high. STR +3 and proficiency +2 should give +5, and the one attack the game rolled used +5 ("11 +5 = 16"), not the sheet's +7.
(2) Speed is 35 ft; a human should have 30.
(3) None of the fighter features appear anywhere: no Second Wind, Action Surge, Fighting Style or Improved Critical.
(4) Equipment never changed. It said "Chain Mail (worn)" and AC 18 while Kell was holding my mail. The page, the wheat-ear crown and the heron token I picked up never appeared on it.
After scene 4 I went up to fighter 4 automatically ("Choices: Ability Score Improvement; +2 to one ability score; Strength"). HP rose to 36/36 and STR to 19; the STR save +6 and Athletics +6 were correct. The attacks then showed +8, which should be +6. "Heroic Inspiration" appeared after the long rest, which is correct for a 2024 human.
scenes_played: 1. The hanged clerk: Caerwyn granary yard and granary interior (turns 1-25, ended 'The case is made')
2. Caerwyn, the afternoon: market square and Corn Exchange, a downtime walk (turns 26-27, ended 'Onward'; an automatic short rest at the start)
3. The Drowned Rat: the tavern, the river stairs, then my walk to the Heron and the confrontation at the river grille (turns 28-44, ended 'Manners' straight after my first punch)
4. The Heron Warehouse (turns 45-48, ended 'Up in smoke'; then an automatic long rest and level-up to 4)
5. The King's Morning: the palace dressing room (turns 49-51, ended 'Done right by' / The End)
report.ended: It ended at turn 51 with "The End. (The session is over.)" in the King's dressing room. The King orders Sallow held for the Assizes, the record says "murder: Wendell Prout", and Moll and Cob are "to be heard, not displayed". It ended as I headed out to fetch Moll myself. The King handed that job to the Marshal and the epilogue summed up the outcomes, so Moll and Cob never spoke to the King on screen.
report.summary:
The story was strong and the rules layer was weak. Scene 1 (the granary yard) was an excellent small murder mystery. The clues came one at a time and each one was earned: the moon-and-rain lie, the dead man's bare feet against Cob's huge boots, a paper crackling in a boot, the cut page that matched the stub, and Prout's note "Not goblins. Who pays the hedge-folk?". The Drowned Rat gave a satisfying payoff: the bandage came off, Hobb confessed, and the cane matched the blow to the skull. The NPCs had distinct, funny voices, and the physical world mostly reacted well. I lowered the body, toppled grain sacks, traded for the crown, and my burning brand set off a grain-dust explosion that burned the Heron. The fire carried into the King's scene.
The D&D side barely appeared: three dice events in 51 turns (Medicine, Persuasion, one Unarmed Strike). Kicking a door, forcing through a gap, a bluff, intimidation, a disarm, a grapple and an explosion all went without rolls. No enemy ever took a turn, so I took no damage in the whole session.
The sheet was wrong in three ways: the attack bonus was +2 too high, removing the mail never changed AC, and picked-up items never appeared. The worst failure was entity and location tracking at the Heron. I punched a newly introduced "broad man in the doorway", and the dice line logged it as "Big Hobb Mallory", the confessed accomplice I had left with Kell at the Drowned Rat. The scene then cut. The next scene's intro reset the Heron (dog snoring, watchman sitting by the brazier), and Kell said both "Hobb is with me" and "he's the man you hit".
Scene cuts also rushed the climax. The grab on Sallow ended the scene, and his custody overnight was never explained.

report.pacing:
Scene 1 was well paced. Each clue was earned by an action (the crate, the bare feet, the boot, the board, the page against the stub). Kell's information came as a reaction, not a dump: "Prout came to the watch house three days ago ... Asked whether I could arrest a gentleman from the Purveyor's office."
Dragging stretches:
- Turns 11-13: three turns at the granary gap. It was "wide enough to squeeze through" at turn 10, "too narrow for your mail" at turn 11, then "force it and risk getting jammed" was offered and refused without a roll.
- Turns 35-37: a custody argument with Kell, with Hobb saying "If I'm not at the Heron by eleven, the Master will know" three times.
Repetitive lines: Moll's "You said nobody'd take anything from him" about five times, and Kell's "What do you want written down?" or "Then tell me what you'll put on the record" three times.
Kell sometimes acted as a hint dispenser: "There may be another way in.", "You've found your man, investigator.", and the invented porter: "The porter also said the big men with bandaged hands drink at the Drowned Rat. We've a call to make."
Hobb went from a hidden hand to the full story ("the Master hit him with his cane and strangled him with a cord") and Sallow's midnight location in four turns. That was quick, but the raw palm earned it.
The back end was rushed:
- Turn 44: the scene ended on my first punch, with the Crakes coming.
- Turn 48: the scene ended the moment I grabbed Sallow. The burning warehouse, the clerk and ledger I sent Kell to save, the gang and the actual arrest were all skipped.
- Turn 51: the story ended in summary when I set off to fetch Moll, so the promised testimony happened off screen.
Sallow, the villain, got one line ("What, precisely, is burning?").
report.characters:
Alive and consistent:
- Sergeant Kell was the stickler throughout: "I won't write 'clubbed' without evidence of a club."; "The Watch feeds us. Eventually. Usually after the danger has passed."; "There's no such authority, investigator." She also had to cover for engine errors ("That's my mistake") and invented the porter.
- Cob kept his third-person voice: "Cob don't talk to bluebottles."; "And Cob can buy his own pie."
- Moll was sharp and protective: "Smells like a flower stall that's been told it's important." She became repetitive.
- Nan the landlady was the best minor character: "Rule three, my duck. No fighting indoors."; "For the stool, my duck. Not the hand."
- Saul: "Duchess says you're trouble, and she knows trouble."
- King Aldren was touching: "Wendell took his tea with the milk first, one sugar, and the cup warmed." and "Prout always disliked heights. He still climbed the tally loft whenever the figures needed him." His voice cooling when I confessed to the fire was a nice touch.
- Hobb: "My mum. You swear it, sir?" A sympathetic accomplice, until the engine also made him the man in the Heron doorway.
Flat:
- Josiah Sallow was never seen properly or confronted.
- Hep Grist and the Crakes were names only.
- The bread seller was funny for one line ("with the air of a man complying with a regrettable regulation").

scene_notes.notes: A strong opener with comic texture (the supervising pigeon, "Spin, you miserable clothes-horse!"). The physical world handled my changes vividly: dragging a crate, toppling sacks, unbarring the loft, lowering the body. Problems: the 'pocketed' stones landed on the cobbles; the gap width contradicted itself; Cob shouted from the yard, then turned out to be the runner I grabbed inside the granary; Moll 'dropped from the wall' twice after already being down; a Persuasion label leaked 'the men in the loft'; and the sheet ignored my armour coming off.

Two turns of nice texture: bunting, the Corn Exchange price board, smaller loaves and Saltmere grain gossip, all tying into the plot. The automatic short rest was harmless. Kell's tip from an unseen porter was a contrivance.

scene_notes.scene: 3 The Drowned Rat (and the walk to the Heron)
scene_notes.notes: The best scene for NPCs: the rules board, Nan's 'Manners', and the bandage reveal and confession. It kept running after I left the Rat, through scouting the Heron and the bluff at the grille. The social checks there got no rolls. It cut away right after the only attack roll of the game, and that roll was logged against Hobb, who was elsewhere.

Its intro replayed the arrival as if I had not just fought at the river door (watchman sitting, dog snoring). Then came the Hobb mix-up ('Hobb is with me' / 'he's the man you hit'). The grain-dust explosion from my brand was a superb physical consequence, but the scene ended the moment I grabbed Sallow.

Charming, and it took my evidence and my confession about the fire seriously. It remembered my promises to Moll and Hobb. It was very short (three turns): it ended as I left to fetch Moll and summarised the rest. Sallow's overnight custody was never explained.

The game offered 'force it and risk getting jammed', then said 'You can't force through in the armour' with no check.
I asked to read the rules board aloud, all of it. Only one rule was quoted ('Gossip sold by the measure'), and 'Rule four' was invoked without being shown.
My bluff at the grille failed outright with no Deception roll.
My intimidation at the grille failed outright with no Intimidation roll.
My attempt to twist the club out of an old man's hand failed outright ('before you can take the club') with no contest.

The scene ended the instant I grabbed Sallow. The burning warehouse, the counting-box clerk and ledger, the gang and the actual arrest and custody were all skipped.
I said I would fetch Moll and Cob myself. The King handed it to the Marshal and the story ended in a summary, so the promised testimony happened off screen.

inconsistencies.what: Moll 'drops from the wall's far side', although in turn 1 she had already 'slid off the wall to the lane side'. In turn 8 her fist 'tightens on the wall's edge' again.
Moll: 'You said Sallow. You said his name.' I never spoke the name aloud.
The gap went from 'wide enough to squeeze through' (turn 10) to 'too narrow for your mail'.
The sheet still said 'Chain Mail (worn)' and AC 18 while Kell was holding the mail.
Cob shouted 'Oi! That's my castle!' from the yard in turn 15, then turned out to be the runner I caught on the granary stairs. The game patched it with 'Got in the same way you did'.
Moll took my two pennies in turn 22 and 'takes the pennies' again in turn 23.
Kell cited 'the porter' as a source, though no porter had appeared. Later she said it was 'One who found the body'.

The dice line named the target 'Big Hobb Mallory' while the story said 'the broad man' in the Heron doorway. Hobb was on the Drowned Rat landing with Kell. The man also 'drops' a sack he had not been carrying.
The attack roll used +5; the sheet says +7 (later +8, where +6 is correct).
The Heron intro had the watchman sitting by the brazier and the dog snoring, minutes after both confronted me at the river door. The gang had been alerted.
Kell said both 'Hobb is with me' and 'And he's the man you hit', and the narrator added 'the doorway attack left Big Hobb hurt inside the warehouse'.
The next morning, with me at the palace, Kell put Sallow 'at the Heron, under Brannoc's hand'. His night was never accounted for.
The sheet gave a human Speed 35 ft (should be 30) and listed no fighter class features.

report.best_moment: Turn 47. I pulled a burning stick from the brazier to stop the loading, and the world played it straight: "'Put that out!' ... For one bright instant the warehouse glows gold. Then the dust flashes." It was followed by Sallow's perfectly pitched arrival line, "What, precisely, is burning?". Next morning the consequence carried over: the Marshal said "The fire is already being reported in the courtyard", and the King's voice "has lost some of its warmth". A close second was turn 18, matching the cut page to the chained book's stub and finding Prout's pencilled note "Not goblins. Who pays the hedge-folk?".
report.worst_moment: Turns 44-46. I punched a newly introduced 'broad man' in the Heron doorway. The dice logged it as "your attack on Big Hobb Mallory ... takes 7 bludgeoning damage", but Hobb was the confessed accomplice I had left with Kell on the Drowned Rat landing. The scene then cut mid-fight, and the next scene re-ran the Heron's arrival with the dog asleep. When I asked, Kell said both "Hobb is with me" and "That's my mistake ... And he's the man you hit." Entity tracking, location tracking, combat and continuity all broke in one exchange.
report.other_notes:
For the request about world-state updates (attributes updated, objects destroyed, new characters placed correctly in the tree, spatial queries like 'nearby'). As a blind tester I saw only effects, not internal state. What those effects suggest:

(1) New characters are not reliably created where they appear. 'A broad man appears in the doorway' at the Heron was resolved to an existing NPC (Hobb) who was at another location. My guess is that the target resolver matches on description ('big man, bandaged hand') rather than on who is actually in the scene. A spatial or location-aware lookup would have prevented it.

(2) NPC positions drift:
- Cob was both in the yard and inside the granary in consecutive turns.
- Moll kept 'dropping from the wall'.
- Kell 'steps into the gap' while I was blocking the gateway.

(3) Things done to or with the player never reach the sheet. Equipment stayed 'Chain Mail (worn)' and AC 18 while the mail was off. Picked-up evidence (page, crown, token) is tracked in the story but not as inventory. Stones I 'pocketed' silently landed on the cobbles instead.

(4) Destruction mostly persisted in the story. The Heron fire carried into the next scene, the cane stayed on the wharf, and Prout's body moved to the cold room. Granary damage (boards, water butt, toppled sacks, the kicked door) was never revisited, so I could not check that it stuck.

(5) Scene openers seem pre-written and are not reconciled with the live world. The Heron intro reset the dog and watchman. The King's scene did not know about the fire until I mentioned it.

(6) 'Nearest crate' was resolved sensibly to 'a porter's empty grain box', so simple nearby-object placement already looks plausible.

Rules summary:
- Only three dice events in 51 turns.
- No enemy turns, no initiative, no damage taken.
- Social checks rolled once (Persuasion) and then skipped (Deception, Intimidation).
- No check for breaking or forcing anything.
- The attack bonus on the sheet is consistently +2 above what the dice use.
- Rests and level-up are automatic at scene changes; the level-up math was correct apart from the attack line.

No command errors occurred. Every turn returned in roughly 5-25 seconds.

run.character: Pip Gallowglass: a silver-tongued con artist and part-time illusionist who claims to be a notary from Pseudopolis
run.persona: You talk, lie, perform and cheat, and use magic for mischief: charm people, cast illusions (a fake noise, a fake wall, a fake you), mock people with spells, disguise yourself. Try to talk your way past every obstacle, and use an illusion at least once to fool someone important. When the dice go against you, play it out. Go ahead of the story when you can: deal with the next problem early and see whether the game keeps up.

report.character_sheet:
Generated as "human bard 3 (College of Lore), criminal background". AC 14, HP 18/18, Initiative +5, Hit Dice 3d8. STR 8, DEX 16, CON 10, INT 14, WIS 12, CHA 15. Spell save DC 12, spell attack +4, slots 1st 4/4 and 2nd 2/2. Cantrips: Minor Illusion, Vicious Mockery. 1st level: Charm Person, Disguise Self, Illusory Script, Silent Image. 2nd level: Detect Thoughts, Suggestion. Expertise in Persuasion (+6) and Insight (+5); Deception +4, Sleight of Hand +5, Stealth +5, and Jack of All Trades on the rest. Equipment: Rapier (in hand), Dagger, Leather Armor.

The numbers check out under 2024/SRD 5.2 rules: standard array with Criminal +2 DEX/+1 INT, the Alert feat (initiative +5), and Rapier +3 with no proficiency because 2024 bards only get simple weapons.

It fitted the concept very well: a con-artist illusionist got exactly the charm, disguise and illusion kit, plus Illusory Script for a fake notary. Quibbles:
- His weapon "in hand" is one he isn't proficient with (the dagger is better at +5).
- He has no coin purse, no instrument and no notary kit or forged papers.
- The ending sheet still listed the dagger I had given away.

At the end I levelled to bard 4: CHA 17 (ASI picked automatically), DC 13, +5, slots 4/3, HP 23, and Heroic Inspiration from the 2024 human trait. All correct, except that no third cantrip and no seventh spell were added.
scenes_played: 1. The hanged clerk: granary yard (Sgt Agnes Kell, Cob, Moll, Wendell Prout's body). Scene end: 'The case is made'
2. Caerwyn, the afternoon: market square, Corn Exchange, bread seller (downtime/transit). Scene end: 'Onward'

3. The Drowned Rat: pub and river stairs (Nan Quill, Big Hobb Mallory, Arlo). I pushed ahead into the Heron warehouse inside this scene (Old Saul, Duchess the dog, clerk Scrope, Master Josiah Sallow, the Crake brothers). Scene end: 'Manners'

report.ended: The game ended cleanly on turn 72 with "The End. (The session is over.)" after The King's Morning. The King ordered Sallow "held for the Assizes. Sergeant Kell's record will say murder", and granted every promise I had made: pies for Cob and Moll, Cob keeps the boots, a kitchen place for Hobb's mother, and Hobb as a Crown witness. Closing line: "Milk first," he says softly. "You remembered."
report.summary:
72 turns as Pip Gallowglass (Lore bard 3, then 4) through six chained scenes.

**What works:** Within a scene the game is strong. NPCs remember promises, gifts and slights and act on them. Spell slots, saving throws, short and long rests and the level-up arithmetic were always booked correctly. Charm Person, Suggestion, Disguise Self, Silent Image and Minor Illusion were played close to the 5e rules ("the spell doesn't make him answer your question"; "Minor Illusion can make the sound, not the sight"). A lantern fire I set kept spreading over many turns: into the mooring ropes, smoke under the eaves, the rope burning through, the barge swinging loose. Two scenes later the rope was still "blackened where it caught".

**What broke:** Getting ahead of the story. I ran the whole Heron confrontation (Sallow arriving at midnight, Hobb confessing in public, the barge breaking loose) inside the Drowned Rat scene. The Rat's scripted ending then fired anyway: Nan Quill, the Rat's landlady, teleported to the Heron's door and threw me out "on the wet stairs". The next two scenes reset the warehouse and replayed "The gentleman comes at midnight to see it off", although NPCs inside still remembered what I'd done.

**Rules and world-state faults:**
- Attacks on the unnamed Crake brothers were rolled and booked against my ally Big Hobb Mallory (11 damage), while the story said the Crakes were hit.
- No initiative was ever rolled.
- Vicious Mockery never rolled a save or damage.
- Most of my Deception and Sleight of Hand attempts were decided without dice.
- The sheet never tracked items. The dagger I gave away stayed listed, and the stone, the evidence and Sallow's cane never appeared.
- At level 4 no cantrip or spell was added.

Fun, funny and warm; consistency is the weak spot.

report.pacing:
**Scene 1** was the best-paced: clues came in a sensible chain (boots, then the paid lie, the body marks, the page in the boot, then Cob's account), gated by two failed Persuasion rolls and an earned apology. The back half gave things up a little easily. Right after the apology Moll volunteered “You want the truth? Start by asking who paid me to lie”, then named Sallow, the cane and the coin in the very next reply. Kell added, unprompted: “Prout came to me three days ago. He asked how to report false entries in the King’s rolls.” Cob then delivered the whole night in one speech (“Then there was a thump. A choking noise. The hoist started creaking.”).

**Kell as prompt:** She often ended a beat with “What would you like to look at first?” / “What do you want me to put on the record, investigator?”, which is a bit hint-dispenser-like.

**Scenes 2 and 3 (the Rat):** Scene 2 was a crisp 4-turn transit. The Rat built real tension with Hobb: he fled, refused (“You don’t know what he’ll do to my mum”), and only confessed after a 17 Persuasion. That felt earned.

**The Heron:** A run of dice-free refusals of my cons (T29 impersonation, T33 grain-sack ride, T38-39 Saltmere notary bluff, T41 'the Watch is coming') felt like the game protecting its plot rather than letting the dice decide.

**Scenes 4-5** dragged because they replayed what I had already done (“The gentleman comes at midnight to see it off”).

**The ending:** The King's Morning paid everything off in 6 turns. It was warm, but slightly rushed: the end card arrived right after I handed over the stone, and the epilogue summarised the fates in one paragraph.
report.characters:
**Sergeant Agnes Kell** is excellent and consistent: dry, scrupulous, and never overawed by my patter.
- “You can ask that their names be withheld. You can’t order it by calling yourself the King’s notary.”
- “Not that way, investigator.”
- “That is not a royal warrant, investigator. It is a page of statements, however convincingly you’ve dressed it.”
- “You do have a history with doors.”

She sometimes doubled as a prompt-giver.

**Cob** was alive: “Interest is two stones. Cob knows numbers.” / “bum-faced palace pigeon”.

**Moll** was sharp: “His Majesty sent a paper-man to stop rocks? That’s a king’s economy for you.” / “Butter knife or not, I know which end to hold.”

**Big Hobb Mallory** was the emotional core: frightened, decent, and believable.
- “You don’t know what he’ll do to my mum.”
- “I only held the rope.”
- “Tell her it’s from her Hobby.”

**Nan Quill** and her cudgel Manners were vivid (“No fighting indoors... Take it to the stairs”), until she was teleported to the Heron.

**Old Saul** was dry and great: “Hobb’s on the hoist, unless he’s stopped being on it. Master’s inside, unless he’s stopped being inside.”

**Scrope** had the best turn of the night: “No, Master. The error is already entered.”

**Hep Grist** appeared late but gave the gang a voice (“We’ll swear. All of us.”).

**King Aldren** was tender and fallible: he admits he set aside Wendell's letter, and closes with “Milk first. You remembered.”

**Weaker characters:**
- **Sallow** is smooth but thin. He leans on procedure (“You will not arrest an officer of the Purveyor’s office without a warrant”) and sees through every trick without a roll.
- **The Crake brothers** (“alike as bollards”) are props with no names or stats, which is likely why my attacks landed on Hobb.
- **Arlo** gets one line.

scene_notes.notes: Strong opening: the stone-throwing boy, the swearing girl, the pigeon, Kell's notebook. The boots clue (Prout in stockings, Cob in oversized black boots) is lovely and paid off with the crackling page in the left boot. My promises (pies, boots, stone with interest) were all tracked. Spells were judged in-world (Kell: “You’ve cast on a witness without asking”). Some auto-resolutions: the stone catch, the palming attempt caught without a roll, the padlock. 17 turns.

Good downtime transit. The short rest was applied correctly, with no bard slot recovery. Worldbuilding was funny (“temporary scarcity is not grounds for discourtesy”). The bread seller handed over the next lead (Saltmere barges, porters with bandaged hands at the Drowned Rat). Kell kept track of my stone and my copper. Disguise Self was handled per the rules. 4 turns.

scene_notes.scene: 3 The Drowned Rat (+ my early trip to the Heron)
scene_notes.notes: 34 turns. The Rat half was excellent: Charm Person, Suggestion and Silent Image were all close to the rules, Hobb was a great NPC, and Nan's rules worked as a mechanic. I then got ahead and went to the Heron in the same scene. The game improvised impressively (Saul, Duchess, Scrope in a glass counting-box, Sallow's arrival, the spreading fire) and NPC memory held. But combat broke (attacks on the Crakes booked to Hobb), and the scene's scripted exit ('Manners') was forced onto the Heron by teleporting Nan and Kell. The brass token was briefly in two places at once.

2 turns. It replayed the pre-Heron setup as if I hadn't been there. When challenged, Kell admitted “I had the order of events wrong” and kept the promise thread (Hobb's mother safe at Nan's). It also kept the false 'Nan put you out' detail.

10 turns. The opening reset the warehouse (loading again, dog asleep), but once engaged everyone remembered me, Hobb's confession and the wounds. Turning Scrope and the gang with Prout's 'proper channels' was the dramatic high point. Kell made the arrest on her own grounds (receiving stolen Crown goods) rather than accept my fake warrant. That was a nice principled beat, but Illusory Script as a ritual was hand-waved.

6 turns. Long rest and level-up handled (with missing spell and cantrip picks). The King's tea detail ran through the scene. All promises were granted explicitly. My Silent Image was cast on an offer and swung the King's decision. Minor staging slips: a dismissed valet and the departed Marshal were still in the room. Ended cleanly and warmly.

report.best_moment:
The fire. At T36 I tipped a lantern into empty sacking at the far end of the wharf as a distraction, and the world kept it burning on its own terms:
- “the fire’s reached the mooring ropes”
- “smoke is beginning to drift beneath the warehouse eaves”
- Sallow charging me with “theft, arson and assault”
- a shout of “It’s through!” as the rope parted, the barge swinging loose, and Hobb grabbing the line with his already rope-burned hands
- two scenes later, “the mooring rope is blackened where it caught”

My own mischief became the turning point of the climax. A close second: Scrope picking up the ledger after I quoted Prout's last words: “No, Master. The error is already entered.”
report.worst_moment: T51 to T56. My rapier attacks on the Crake brothers were rolled and booked against my ally Big Hobb Mallory, with the narration even saying “Your rapier lunges for Hobb’s reaching forearm”. Then Nan Quill, the landlady of a different building, materialised at the Heron to throw me out so the Drowned Rat scene could end on its scripted beat. The next two scenes then reset the warehouse and told me “The gentleman comes at midnight to see it off”, after I had already confronted him at midnight and got a public confession.
report.other_notes:
**What looks tracked as real state, and what looks narrative-only.** These observations bear on the user's goal of world updates applied to a state tree (items destroyed, new characters added to the tree, spatial queries such as 'nearby' or 'radius'). I played blind, so they are inferences from behaviour.

Tracked as real state:
- HP, spell slots, spell durations, rests and level
- The 'charmed' condition on Hobb
- Damage on named NPCs

Narrative-only:
- **Items.** The given-away dagger stayed on the sheet. The pocketed stone, sacking, grain and the confiscated cane never appeared. Money doesn't exist, yet I could spend a copper.
